platform_notes: Our sheets and Dejavoo's own pages put the P line on Dejavoo's gateway payment app (DvPay) managed through the iPOSpays portal, with SPIn for POS integration; the P18 can instead run DejaPay Pro. Dejavoo's P-line quick reference guide gives the manager password as the last 4 digits of the TPN. One reseller guide (PaymentCloud, P3) describes an older CREDIT/DEBIT menu build with password 1234.

entries.title: What the icons on the idle screen do
steps: The idle screen shows the payment screen plus a set of icons.
One icon opens the FAVORITES menu.
One icon opens the CORE menu.
One icon is the CALL ME feature.
One icon downloads the quick reference guide.
entries.quote: As well as the payment screen, the terminal’s idle screen also displays the following icons:
entries.note: The PDF version of the same guide labels the second icon 'Access to other sales features' instead of the CORE menu.

entries.title: Run a credit card sale
steps: Enter the sale amount and press Ok.
Review the amount and tap Proceed.
Tap Cash Payment or Card Payment. The price is based on the payment type.
Have the customer tap (contactless only), swipe or insert the chip card.
Depending on how the terminal is set up, choose how to send the customer copy: SMS, email, paper print or no receipt.
The transaction is processed and the sales receipt prints.
entries.quote: Tap (contactless only), swipe or insert chip card.
entries.note: The guide is written for the whole P line; steps that mention printing apply only to models with a printer.

entries.title: Why the terminal asks Cash Payment or Card Payment
steps: During a sale the terminal asks you to choose Cash Payment or Card Payment.
Tap the one the customer is using.
The price charged is based on the payment type you choose.
entries.quote: Chose Cash Payment or Card Payment by tapping option. Pricing will be based on payment type.

entries.title: Receipt choices after a sale: SMS, email, paper or none
steps: After a sale the terminal can offer to send the customer copy by SMS, by email, as a paper print, or not at all.
Which choices appear depends on how the terminal's TPN is configured.
entries.quote: Depending on TPN configuration, you will have the option to send customer copy as SMS, email, paper print or no receipt.
entries.review: routed to support by rule: steps need staff access

entries.title: Run a debit sale
steps: Enter the sale amount and press Ok.
Review the amount and tap Proceed.
Tap Cash Payment or Card Payment. The price is based on the payment type.
Tap the Debit icon, then have the customer tap (contactless only), insert or swipe the card.
The customer enters their PIN on the terminal or on the PIN pad and presses Enter.
The transaction is processed and the sales receipt prints.
entries.quote: Tap on Debit icon and then tap (contactless only), insert or swipe card.
entries.note: The guide is written for the whole P line; steps that mention printing apply only to models with a printer.

entries.title: Refund (return) a credit card sale
steps: Tap the menu icon on the terminal home screen.
Tap the Refund icon.
Enter the password. The default password is the last 4 digits of your TPN.
Enter the return amount and press Ok.
Have the customer tap (contactless only) or insert the chip card.
Depending on how the terminal is set up, choose how to send the customer copy: SMS, email, paper print or no receipt.
The return is processed and the return receipt prints.
entries.quote: Tap on the Refund icon. Enter Password (default password is last 4 digits of your TPN).
entries.note: The guide is written for the whole P line; steps that mention printing apply only to models with a printer.
entries.review: routed to support by rule: steps need staff access

entries.title: Key in a card number by hand (card not present)
steps: Enter the sale amount and press Ok.
Review the amount and tap Proceed.
Tap Card Payment. The price is based on the payment type.
Tap Enter Card under other options.
Type in the card number.
Follow the prompts, such as expiry date and ZIP code. Which prompts appear depends on the terminal's configuration.
Depending on how the terminal is set up, choose how to send the customer copy.
The transaction is processed and the sales receipt prints.
entries.quote: Follow the CNP prompts (input exp. date, ZIP code etc). Conditional on the terminal’s configuration.
entries.note: The guide is written for the whole P line; steps that mention printing apply only to models with a printer.

entries.title: Void a credit transaction
steps: Tap the menu icon on the terminal home screen.
Tap the Void icon.
Enter the transaction number or the last 4 digits of the card.
Choose the transaction from the list, tap Confirm, then tap Yes.
If asked, enter the password. The default password is the last 4 digits of your TPN.
The void completes and the terminal offers the receipt options.
entries.quote: Input the Transaction Number or last 4 digits of the card, choose transaction from the list and tap Confirm prompt and tap Yes.
entries.review: routed to support by rule: steps need staff access

entries.title: A void does not need the customer's card
steps: You can void a transaction without the card being present.
Find the transaction by its transaction number or by the last 4 digits of the card.
entries.quote: Note: Card doesn’t need to be present to complete void successfully.

entries.title: Reprint a receipt
steps: Tap the star icon to open the Favorites menu.
Tap Reprint Receipt.
If asked, enter the password. The default password is the last 4 digits of your TPN.
Enter the transaction number or the last 4 digits of the card number.
Select the transaction.
Follow the prompts and the receipt prints.
entries.quote: enter transaction # or last 4 digits of card #, select transaction and tap.
entries.note: The guide is written for the whole P line; steps that mention printing apply only to models with a printer.
entries.review: routed to support by rule: steps need staff access

entries.title: Ask for a call back from the help desk (Call Me)
steps: This feature must be enabled on your terminal.
Tap the phone icon.
Tap Call Me under the Support Menu and choose a reason.
Enter your call back number.
The terminal notifies the help desk and a representative calls you back.
entries.quote: Tap Call Me, under the Support Menu and choose reason. Enter your call back number.

entries.title: Add or change a tip on a transaction (Adjust Tip)
steps: Tap the star icon to open the Favorites menu.
Tap Adjust Tip.
If asked, enter the password. The default password is the last 4 digits of your TPN.
Enter the transaction number, or scroll or swipe through the transactions.
Tap the transaction number.
Tap the button to submit, then tap Yes when asked if you want to submit the tip adjust.
A screen confirms the tip adjust succeeded.
entries.quote: a prompt will appear asking if you want to submit tip adjust, tap Yes. A screen will appear confirming the success of the procedure.
entries.review: routed to support by rule: steps need staff access

entries.title: Settle the daily batch
steps: Tap the star icon to open the Favorites menu.
Tap Show/Settle Daily Batch.
If asked, enter the password. The default password is the last 4 digits of your TPN.
The terminal fetches and shows a summary report. Swipe left to see a detailed report.
Tap the Settle button in the top right corner.
If a prompt about untipped transactions appears, answer Yes or No to continue.
The settlement report prints.
entries.quote: The terminal will fetch and display a summary report. Swipe left to view a detailed report.
entries.note: The guide is written for the whole P line; steps that mention printing apply only to models with a printer.
entries.review: routed to support by rule: steps need staff access

entries.title: Settling shows a prompt about untipped transactions
steps: When you tap Settle, a prompt may appear if some transactions have no tip.
Answer Yes or No to continue with the settlement.
To add the tips first, use Adjust Tip in the Favorites menu before settling.
entries.quote: A prompt may appear if there are untipped transactions. Answer Yes or No to continue to settle.

entries.title: Print a report (open batch or closed batch)
steps: Tap the star icon to open the Favorites menu.
Tap Reports.
Choose Open Batch or Closed Batch.
Tap the report type you want and choose how the report groups your transactions (summary report or daily report).
Tap Next.
Swipe left to go from the summary to the details report, then tap the print icon.
The report prints.
entries.quote: Tap desired report type, select how you want the report to group your transactions. For summary report or daily report. Tap Next.
entries.note: The guide is written for the whole P line; steps that mention printing apply only to models with a printer.

entries.title: Power off or reboot the terminal
steps: Press and hold the button on the side of the terminal until a menu appears on the screen.
The menu offers Power Off and Reboot.
Tap the one you want.
entries.quote: hold until a menu appears on the screen, with the following options: Power Off, Reboot.

entries.title: Wi-Fi icon is blinking
steps: A blinking Wi-Fi icon means the terminal is not connected to Wi-Fi.
When the terminal is connected, the icon stays still.
entries.quote: Wi-Fi icon will blink when not connected. It will remain static when connected successfully.

entries.title: Connect by Ethernet cable
steps: Plug the terminal into power first.
Then plug an Ethernet cable into the terminal's Ethernet port.
entries.quote: To get an internet connection via ethernet, first plug the device into power and then use an ethernet cable to plug into the ethernet port.
entries.note: Applies only to P-line models that have an Ethernet port.

entries.title: Default password on P-line terminals: last 4 digits of the TPN
steps: When the terminal asks for a password for a refund, void, reprint, tip adjust or settlement, the default is the last 4 digits of your TPN.
entries.quote: If prompted, enter Password (default password is last 4 digits of your TPN).
entries.note: PaymentCloud's P3 guide gives 1234 instead; see the separate tier 2 entry.
entries.review: routed to support by rule: steps need staff access

entries.title: Debit sale: receipt options appear after the PIN is entered
steps: After the customer enters the PIN and presses Enter, the terminal may offer to send the customer copy by SMS, email, paper print or no receipt, depending on the TPN configuration.
Then the transaction is processed and the sales receipt prints.
entries.quote: Customer enters PIN on encrypted terminal or on encrypted PIN Pad and press Enter.

entries.title: Pair a P terminal as a PIN pad to a main terminal
steps: On the main screen, tap the red gear at the bottom left corner.
Enter your password to open settings.
Tap PinPad.
Follow the pairing instructions shown on that screen.
entries.quote: Enter your password to access settings, tap on PinPad. You will find the instructions on how to pair.

entries.title: PIN pad will not pair or connect to the main terminal
steps: Make sure both terminals are connected to the same network.
If the site has extenders and routers, select the same one on both devices.
For example, if the main terminal is on the main router, the PIN pad cannot be on the extender.
entries.quote: Make sure both terminals are connected to the same network. If you have extenders/channels and routers, make sure you select the same one for both devices.

entries.title: Which P terminals can act as a PIN pad or main terminal
steps: Dejavoo states that all P terminal hardware combinations can be used as PIN pads and as master terminals.
entries.quote: All P terminal hardwares combinations can be used as PinPads and master terminals.
entries.note: PayCompass (tier 2) says the P5 and P8 do not support external PIN pads; the two sources differ.

entries.title: Load a paper roll in the P3
steps: Hold the device in both hands.
Pinch the sides of the top of the device, next to the card tap section.
Flip the top away from the device screen.
Put the receipt paper into the slot of the printer. The guide says the paper size should be about 50 ft.
Pull out some paper so the end is left outside, then close the top.
entries.quote: Flip the top away from the device screen.

entries.title: Turn the P3 on or off
steps: Press and hold the POWER button on the side of the terminal until a menu appears.
The menu offers POWER OFF, REBOOT, AIRPLANE MODE and SILENT MODE.
Select the option you want.
entries.quote: OFF, REBOOT, AIRPLANE MODE, and SILENT MODE.

entries.title: Set up the network connection on the P3 (PaymentCloud's steps)
steps: Tap the gear icon on the main menu.
Enter the manager password. This guide gives 1234.
Select COMM SETUP.
Select your network of choice.
Tap GPRS.
Enter the password if asked; the terminal then configures the connection.
entries.quote: Enter the password if prompted, after which it will configure.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's P3 guide. It describes a build with CREDIT/DEBIT menus and manager password 1234, which differs from Dejavoo's own P-line guide (last 4 digits of the TPN); the merchant's software build may not match.

entries.title: P3 default password according to PaymentCloud: 1234
steps: PaymentCloud's P3 guide states the default password is 1234.
entries.quote: The default password for the Dejavoo P3 is 1234
entries.note: Disagrees with Dejavoo's P-line quick reference guide (last 4 digits of the TPN) and with PaymentCloud's own download steps for the same P3, which ask for the last 4 digits of the TPN.

entries.title: Register a SIM card for 4G service (Dejavoo Systems portal)
steps: Open the Dejavoo Systems portal.
Select your monthly plan. An AT&T SIM needs an AT&T plan; a Verizon SIM needs a Verizon plan.
Choose your subscription plan from the drop-down menu.
Enter your email address and create a password.
Enter your credit card details.
Enter your billing address, or tick the box if it is the same as your postal address.
Enter your billing contact phone number.
Tick the box to agree to the terms and conditions.
When everything is filled in, the INCOMPLETE button changes to SIGN-UP. Click SIGN-UP.
A window confirms the account was created.
Check your email for instructions on setting up your service.
entries.quote: must choose an AT&T monthly plan. If you have a Verizon
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's P3 guide. SIM plans carry a monthly charge; ask before signing up.

entries.note: The guide shows the on-terminal steps, but a download should be done with tech support. The guide says the download brings the required firmware, software and encryption keys after the Terminal Profile Number is set up.

entries.title: Change the date and time on the P3 (PaymentCloud's steps)
steps: From the idle screen, press OK to open the Core Menu.

If the date shown is correct press OK. If not, clear it with the yellow backspace key and enter the date as MM/DD/YY.
If the time shown is correct press OK. If not, clear it with the yellow backspace key and enter the time in 24-hour format.
The terminal returns to the settings menu.

entries.title: Reboot the P3 (troubleshooting tip)
steps: Find the small button on the side of the P3 marked with a dash inside a circle and press it.

entries.quote: You will then be presented with the following options: POWER

entries.title: Factory reset the P3 (erases everything)
steps: Do not start this without support: the guide warns a factory reset erases all data on the device, including transaction history and customized settings.
The guide's steps are: swipe down from the top of the screen and open the Android settings gear.
Select About Device at the bottom of the screen.
Tap Custom Build Version 6 times.
Select the Dialer.
Enter *#87#.
Select Factory Reset.
entries.quote: Note: Performing a factory reset will erase all data on the device,
entries.note: PaymentCloud's P5 guide adds that if a factory reset is done incorrectly Dejavoo will not be able to reinstall the app. Treat as a tech-support procedure.

entries.title: Who PaymentCloud's P3 guide says to contact about the terminal

entries.quote: Dejavoo terminal, contact Dejavoo directly, either via email

entries.title: The P5 has no printer and takes no paper
steps: The P5 has no built-in receipt printer, so there is no paper roll to load.
It cannot print or reprint customer receipts, and it cannot print reports.
Send receipts by email or text instead.
entries.quote: The Dejavoo P5 has no built-in printer and cannot print reports.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's P5 guide (tier 2); the merchant's software build may differ.

entries.title: Reprinting a receipt is not possible on the P5

entries.note: From PaymentCloud's P5 guide (tier 2); the merchant's software build may differ.

Enter the return amount, then confirm.
Send the customer a receipt by email or text if wanted.
entries.quote: When prompted to select a method for the refund, select
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's P5 guide (tier 2); the merchant's software build may differ.

entries.title: Void a credit transaction on the P5 (card present or not)
steps: Open the MENU on the P5.
Select VOID.
Enter either the last four digits of the card used or the transaction number.
If asked, enter the manager password.
The void is processed, with the option to send a receipt by text or email.
entries.quote: VOID will then be processed, with the option to send a
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's P5 guide (tier 2); the merchant's software build may differ. The guide gives the same steps for card present and card not present.

entries.title: Change the date and time on the P5
steps: Open the MENU on the P5.
If asked, select UTILITY.
Select SETTINGS.
Select DATE AND TIME.
If the date and time shown are right, leave them. If not, clear them and re-enter.
Enter the date as MM/DD/YY.
Enter the time in 24-hour format.
entries.quote: Find and select the DATE AND TIME option.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's P5 guide (tier 2); the merchant's software build may differ.

entries.title: Change menu security settings on the P5
steps: Open the MENU on the P5.
If asked, select UTILITY.
Select SECURITY.
Select MENU UTILITY.
Choose the security option you want.
entries.quote: Choose your desired security option.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's P5 guide (tier 2); the merchant's software build may differ.

entries.title: Adjust the display contrast on the P5
steps: Open the MENU on the P5.
If asked, select UTILITY.
Select SETTINGS.
Select DISPLAY.
Tap + to increase contrast or - to decrease it.
Save your settings.
entries.quote: Tap + to increase display contrast or - to decrease contrast.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's P5 guide (tier 2); the merchant's software build may differ.

entries.title: Factory reset on a P-line terminal: do not do it without support
steps: Do not factory reset the terminal on your own.
The guide warns that if a factory reset is performed incorrectly, Dejavoo will not be able to reinstall the app on the device.
It also says that if the terminal is then sent back for repair, Dejavoo reserves the right not to swap it.
Contact support for help instead.
entries.quote: not be able to reinstall the app onto that customer’s device. If the
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's P5 guide (tier 2); the merchant's software build may differ. The guide names the P1, P3 and P5 as examples of P line terminals.

entries.title: Factory reset the P5 from Android settings (guide's steps)
steps: This is a support procedure; see the warning entry before attempting it.
On the P5 screen, select ANDROID SETTINGS.
Select ABOUT DEVICE at the bottom of the screen.
Tap HARDWARE VERSION or CUSTOM BUILD VERSION 6 to 8 times, depending on the terminal.
Select the DIALER.
Enter *#87#.
The device begins its factory reset.
If prompted, download the TPN.
entries.quote: VERSION. This step must be completed anywhere from 6-8 times
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's P5 guide (tier 2); the merchant's software build may differ.

entries.title: Factory reset from Android Recovery mode (guide's alternative)
steps: This is a support procedure; see the warning entry before attempting it.
Press and hold the POWER and VOLUME buttons together for about ten to fifteen seconds.
The device may go into Android Recovery mode.
Select WIPE DATA/FACTORY RESET, then confirm.
The device begins its factory reset.
entries.quote: Recovery mode. Following this, select WIPE DATA/FACTORY RESET,
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's P5 guide (tier 2); the merchant's software build may differ.

entries.title: Reboot the P5 (troubleshooting tip)
steps: Find the small button on the side of the P5 marked with a dash inside a circle and press it.
The screen offers POWER OFF or REBOOT.
Select REBOOT.
entries.quote: A small button on the side of your Dejavoo P5 will display a dash
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's P5 guide (tier 2); the merchant's software build may differ.

entries.title: The P17 is powered over USB from the P1
steps: Dejavoo describes the P17 as USB-powered through the P1 terminal.
A single USB connection means the pad needs no power adapter of its own.
entries.quote: Single USB connection eliminates power adapter requirements and reduces cable clutter for cleaner workspaces

entries.title: P17 Wi-Fi is 2.4GHz
steps: Dejavoo's product page lists the P17's connectivity as Wi-Fi 2.4GHz, a USB Type-C port and an audio jack.
entries.quote:
WiFi: 2.4GHz
USB Type-C port and audio jack
entries.note: Our sheet says the P17 flyer names no Wi-Fi band; the product page names 2.4GHz only.

entries.title: Card types the P17 reads
steps: The P17 supports chip (IC), contactless (NFC) and magstripe cards.
Listed contactless methods are Paypass (Mastercard), Paywave (Visa), Expresspay (AMEX) and D-PAS (Discover).
entries.quote: Payment Methods: Paypass (MC), Paywave (Visa), Expresspay

entries.title: The P17 works with CloudPOS
steps: Dejavoo lists CloudPOS compatibility for the P17.
entries.quote: CloudPOS compatibility provides scalability and advanced business management capabilities

entries.title: The P12 charging cradle is a separate purchase
steps: The P12's cradle is sold separately.
entries.quote: *Cradle sold separately.

entries.title: Card types the P12 reads: chip, tap and QR code
steps: Dejavoo's P12 flyer lists its payment readers as an IC (chip) card reader, an NFC (tap) reader and QR code.
It works with digital wallets including Apple Pay, Google Wallet and Samsung Pay.
entries.quote: IC Card reader, NFC reader, QR Code
entries.note: The flyer does not list a magnetic stripe reader for the P12. Our sheet calls the P12 a 'swiper'.

entries.title: What the P12 is: a standalone Android mPOS / PIN pad
steps: Dejavoo describes the P12 as an Android mPOS/PIN Pad with a 4-inch touchscreen.
It runs an Android-based system and is compatible with iPOSpays, SPIn and DeNovo.
entries.quote: iPOSpay, SPIn, and DeNovo business management tools
entries.note: Our sheet describes the P12 as a reader paired to the merchant's phone through an app; the maker's page describes a touchscreen Android terminal.

entries.title: How the P12 connects: dual-band Wi-Fi, cellular, Bluetooth
steps: The P12 has dual-band Wi-Fi (2.4GHz and 5GHz).
It supports 2G/3G/4G cellular networks.
It has Bluetooth 4.2.
entries.quote: Dual-band Wi-Fi (2.4GHz and 5GHz) Cellular Network: 2G/3G/4G

entries.title: Cellular on the P12 is an optional configuration
steps: The P12 can support cellular data, but PayCompass notes this is an optional configuration.
If a P12 will not connect over cellular, check whether the unit was ordered with cellular.
entries.quote: NOTE: While the P12 does support cellular data (2G, 3G,4G), it's an optional configuration.

entries.title: Receipts on the P12: email, SMS or none; paper only with a separate printer
steps: The P12 offers email, SMS or no receipt.
A paper receipt is available only when the P12 is paired with a separate printer.
entries.quote: Paper receipt option is available when the P12 is paired with a separate printer

entries.title: Optional PIN pad for the P12: the P17
steps: PayCompass lists the Dejavoo P17 as the optional PIN pad for the P12.
entries.quote: Optional PIN Pad: Yes, the Dejavoo P17 PIN Pad

entries.title: The P12 does not capture signatures
steps: PayCompass lists signature capture as not available on the P12.
Tips are supported.
entries.quote:
Signature capture:  No
Receipt options: Email, SMS, or no receipt.

entries.title: How the P18 connects: Ethernet, 4G/LTE, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth
steps: The P18 supports Ethernet, 4G/LTE, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth 5.2.
It takes a Nano SIM.
entries.quote: Ethernet, 4G/LTE, Wi-Fi, Nano SIM, Nano SAM, Bluetooth 5.2

entries.title: The P18 runs Android 13
steps: Dejavoo lists the P18's software as Android 13.
entries.quote:
> SOFTWARE
Android 13
> PROCESSOR

entries.title: The P18's second screen shows the amount to the customer
steps: The P18 has a hidden second screen that displays transaction amounts to the customer.
entries.quote: features a hidden second screen that displays transaction amounts creating a unique checkout experience for customers

entries.title: Payment types the P18 accepts
steps: The P18 supports chip (IC), contactless (NFC), magstripe cards, QR code, digital wallets and Apple Pay.
entries.quote: Supports: IC, NFC, Magstripe Card, QR code, Digital wallet, Apple Pay

entries.title: The P18 has no built-in printer; use an external one
steps: The P18 does not have a built-in printer.
Receipts can go by email, SMS or digital link.
An external printer can be connected by Bluetooth, Wi-Fi or Ethernet cable.
entries.quote: Although the P18 does not have a built-in printer, it can accommodate an external printer by connecting either via Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, or ethernet cable.

entries.title: Optional PIN pad for the P18: the P17
steps: PayCompass lists the Dejavoo P17 Android PIN Pad as the optional PIN pad for the P18.
entries.quote: Optional PIN Pad: Yes, specifically the Dejavoo P17 Android PIN Pad

entries.title: Fleet cards on the P18 need to be set up first
steps: The P18 does not take fleet cards out of the box.
PayCompass says it has to be configured by the processor to accept WEX, Voyager, Fuelman, Comdata and Fleet One.
If a fleet card will not go through, ask whether fleet acceptance was set up on the account.
entries.quote: Fleet cards: Yes, but not natively.
entries.note: PayCompass is describing its own accounts; whether we offer this must be confirmed.

entries.title: Receipts on the P5: email and SMS only
steps: The P5 has no built-in receipt printer.
Receipts are sent by email or SMS.
entries.quote: Receipt options: Email & SMS only; no built-in receipt printer

entries.title: The P5 does not take an external PIN pad (per PayCompass)
steps: PayCompass states the P5 does not support external PIN pads.
entries.quote: Optional PIN Pad: The P5 does not support external PIN pads
entries.note: Dejavoo's own pin pad page says all P terminal combinations can be used as PIN pads and master terminals; the sources differ.

entries.title: The P8 does not take an external PIN pad (per PayCompass)
steps: PayCompass states the P8 does not support external PIN pads.
entries.quote: Optional PIN Pad: No, the P8 does not support external PIN pads
entries.note: Dejavoo's own pin pad page says all P terminal combinations can be used as PIN pads and master terminals; the sources differ.

entries.title: Receipt options on the P8
steps: The P8 can give a paper receipt, an email receipt, an SMS receipt or no receipt.
PayCompass lists signature capture as not available on the P8.
entries.quote: Receipt options: Paper, email, SMS, or no receipt

entries.title: P1 receipt options and optional PIN pad
steps: The P1 can give a paper receipt, an email receipt, an SMS receipt or no receipt.
Its optional PIN pad is the P17.
It connects by Ethernet and Wi-Fi.
entries.quote: Optional PIN Pad: Yes, the P17 PIN Pad

entries.title: The P3 has no Ethernet; it uses cellular and Wi-Fi
steps: PayCompass lists the P3's connectivity as USB charger, cellular and Wi-Fi, with no Ethernet.
Its optional PIN pad is the Dejavoo P17.
entries.quote: Connectivity: USB charger, Cellular & Wi-Fi; no ethernet
entries.note: PaymentCloud's P3 guide titles its network section 'Ethernet or Wifi'; PayCompass says the P3 has no Ethernet.

entries.title: Dejavoo's own tech support line
steps: Dejavoo's tech support page gives the number 1-877-358-6797, option 2.
entries.quote:
Call us 
1-877-358-6797 option 2
entries.note: For issues only the maker can resolve; our tech support is the first contact.

entries.title: Changing the TPN on the terminal needs a one-time passcode
steps: A one-time passcode (OTP) is required to change the Terminal Profile Number (TPN) on a terminal.
This is not something to do yourself; contact support if the terminal is asking to change or re-enter its TPN.
entries.quote: a one-time passcode (OTP) is now required to change the Terminal Profile Number (TPN) on a POS terminal

entries.title: Incremental Auth: raise the amount of a pre-auth
steps: On gateway-powered terminals, Incremental Auth lets you increase the amount first authorized in a Pre-Auth.
entries.quote: Merchants using Gateway-powered terminals can utilize Incremental Auth to increase the amount initially authorized in a Pre-Auth.

entries.title: "Spring Framework" error during Incremental Auth
steps: This error appeared on Dejavoo payment terminals during an Incremental Auth.
Dejavoo fixed it in a software update.
If you still see it, contact support so the terminal's software can be updated.
entries.quote: This update resolves an issue where a "Spring Framework" error would appear on the merchant’s Dejavoo payment terminal

entries.title: See untipped and server reports for other terminals in the same store
steps: From one terminal, you can view untipped and server reports of the other TPNs within the same store.
entries.quote: This update enables merchants to view untipped and server reports of other TPNs within the same store from a single terminal.

entries.title: Tip Adjust by Store: adjust tips for several terminals from one device
steps: Merchants can adjust the tip for multiple TPNs from a single device or batch.
All the TPNs must be within the same store.
entries.quote: adjust the tip for multiple TPNs from a single device or batch, as long as all TPNs are within the same store

entries.title: Two settlement report emails arrived for one batch
steps: In some instances merchants received duplicate settlement reports by email after settling a batch.
Dejavoo says a software update addresses this.
entries.quote: merchants received duplicate settlement reports via email after settling a batch

entries.title: What the batch settlement report shows
steps: Batch settlement reports include Card Brand, Subtotal and Fee details.
entries.quote: Batch settlement reports now include Card Brand, Subtotal, and Fee details.

entries.title: Tip screen: tapping a suggested tip moves straight to the next screen
steps: On gateway-powered terminals, when the customer taps one of the tip choices the app goes to the next screen.
entries.quote: when a user taps on any of the tip choices, the app will take them to the next screen

entries.title: PIN pad transactions ask before printing the customer copy
steps: When the Customer Copy Print option is enabled, the merchant is asked to confirm printing the customer copy during PIN pad transactions.
entries.quote: Merchants are now prompted to confirm printing the customer copy during PIN pad transactions when the Customer Copy Print option is enabled.
